lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: why all circles are similar

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 20°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
4, because the tangent bisects the radius
8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 180°, in terms of π.
choices: arc 3π; sector 9/2π
arc 3π; sector 9π
arc 3/2π; sector 9/2π
arc 9/2π; sector 3π

items.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 74°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 28°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 7. From an external point 25 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 24, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
24, because the tangent bisects the radius
18, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
32, because the tangent extends beyond the circle

items.prompt: A circle has radius 15. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 45°, in terms of π.
choices: arc 15/4π; sector 225/4π
arc 15/4π; sector 225/8π
arc 225/8π; sector 15/4π
arc 15/8π; sector 225/8π

items.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 127°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 154°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
